title: Mermaid diagrams (.mmd, .mermaid)
summary: A Mermaid flowchart, sequence diagram, class diagram, state diagram, entity relationship diagram, pie chart, or gantt chart is laid out like Mermaid 11 and drawn as one still picture with the bundled fonts.

items.text: Flowcharts: the flowchart and graph keywords with the directions TB, TD, BT, LR, and RL, laid out with a port of Mermaid's dagre layout, so the nodes, edges, and labels land where Mermaid 11 puts them.

Node shapes: every bracket form ([ ], ( ), ([ ]), [[ ]], [( )], (( )), ((( ))), > ], { } and its doubled form (a hexagon), [/ /], [\ \], [/ \], [\ /]) and the @{ shape: ... } syntax with all of Mermaid's named shapes (rect, rounded, stadium, cyl, diam, hex, doc, docs, fork, delay, and so on).

Links: arrows, open links, dotted (-.->) and thick (==>) links, circle and cross heads, two-headed links, links of any length (--->), labels (-- text --> and -->|text|), chains and & groups (a & b --> c), invisible links (~~~), self-loops, and edge ids with curve and animate shape data (an animated edge is drawn as its first frame).
Subgraphs: titles, nesting, their own direction, links to and from a subgraph.
Labels: quoted text, Markdown strings ("`**bold** and *italic*`"), HTML line breaks and the common inline tags, entity codes, and wrapping at Mermaid's width.

Styles: style, classDef (including classDef default), class, :::, linkStyle (including default and interpolate), with fill, stroke, stroke-width, stroke-dasharray, color, font-weight, font-style, font-size, font-family, and opacity.

Configuration: YAML frontmatter (title, config), %%{init: ...}%% directives, the five themes (default, base, dark, forest, neutral), themeVariables, and the flowchart settings (nodeSpacing, rankSpacing, curve, padding, wrappingWidth, and so on), with Mermaid's precedence.

Sequence diagrams: a sequence diagram starts with sequenceDiagram. It is laid out by a port of Mermaid's sequence renderer: the participants stand in a row in the order they appear, and every message, note, activation, and block is placed below the one before it, where Mermaid 11 puts it.
Participants: participant and actor, aliases (participant Bank as Payment provider), and participants named only by a message.
Participant types: the eight types of @{ type: ... }: participant, actor, boundary, control, entity, database, collections, and queue, with the alias key.
Boxes: box with a color and a title (box LightBlue Front end ... end), with a color only, or with a title only.
Create and destroy: create participant and create actor just before the first message of the participant, and destroy just before its last message.
Messages: the arrows ->, -->, ->>, -->>, <<->>, <<-->>, -x, --x, -), and --), the half-arrow heads, self messages, and central connections (A->>()B, A()->>B, A()->>()B).

The half-arrow heads draw one side of a head: -|\ and -|/ draw a solid half head at the top or at the bottom, and -\\ and -// a stick half head; with -- the line is dotted (--|\, --//, and so on). Written before the line, they point back at the sender: /|-, \|-, //-, and \\-, and the dotted /|--, \|--, //--, and \\--.
Activations: activate and deactivate, and the + and - shorthands on a message, nested.
Notes: Note left of, right of, and over one or two participants.
Blocks: loop, alt and else, opt, par and and, par_over, critical and option, and break, nested; rect backgrounds with a CSS color.
Numbers: autonumber, with a start and a step, and autonumber off; the showSequenceNumbers setting.

Text:
line breaks, the wrap: and nowrap: prefixes, wrapping when wrap is on (a word wider than the line is hyphenated), and entity codes.
Menus and properties: link, links, and properties; a menu is drawn only with forceMenus, and a class in properties changes the paint of the participant.
A hidden menu still takes its room: the diagram is as large as if the menu panel below the participant (20 pixels plus 30 per link, and as wide as its widest label) were drawn.

The lines of a menu link label are drawn on one baseline when the participant font size has a unit, such as an actorFontSize of 18px with the top-level fontSize set to 0, because Mermaid spaces them by the size as a number.

Configuration: YAML frontmatter, %%{init: ...}%% directives, the five themes, themeVariables, and the sequence settings (actorMargin, mirrorActors, rightAngles, messageAlign, noteAlign, wrap, and so on), with Mermaid's precedence. As in Mermaid, the top-level fontFamily and fontSize replace the font families and sizes of the sequence settings, so every sequence text is 16 pixels in the theme's font by default; set the top-level fontSize to change it. A top-level fontWeight replaces the three weights in the same way.

Pictures: an @{ img: "part.png", label, pos, w, h, constraint } node shows a raster, an SVG file, an OpenSCAD model, a Vega-Lite chart, a page of a PDF, PPTX, or VSDX document, or another diagram that lies beside the diagram (see the pictures example). At most {{mmdMaxImages}} pictures.
Titles: the title statement, else the frontmatter title, is drawn above the diagram; accTitle and accDescr are read as metadata.

Class diagrams: a class diagram starts with classDiagram. It is laid out with the same port of Mermaid's dagre layout as a flowchart, so the class boxes, relations, namespaces, and notes land where Mermaid 11 puts them; its syntax, relations, and settings are listed under Class diagrams.

State diagrams: a state diagram starts with stateDiagram-v2 or stateDiagram. It is laid out with the same port of Mermaid's dagre layout as a flowchart, so the states, transitions, composite states, and notes land where Mermaid 11 puts them; its syntax and settings are listed under State diagrams.

Entity relationship diagrams: an entity relationship diagram starts with erDiagram. It is laid out with the same port of Mermaid's dagre layout as a flowchart, so the entities, relationships, and subgraphs land where Mermaid 11 puts them; its syntax, cardinalities, and settings are listed under Entity relationship diagrams.

Pie charts: a pie chart starts with pie. It is drawn by a port of Mermaid's pie renderer, so the slices, the percentage labels, the legend, and the title land where Mermaid 11 puts them; its syntax and settings are listed under Pie charts.

Gantt charts: a gantt chart starts with gantt. It is drawn by a port of Mermaid's gantt renderer, with the time scale and the axis of d3, so the bars, the texts, the section rows, and the ticks land where Mermaid 11 puts them, with the dates in UTC; its syntax, tags, and settings are listed under Gantt charts.

info reports the type, direction, titles, and the numbers of nodes, edges, and subgraphs (participants, messages, and boxes for a sequence diagram; classes, relations, and namespaces for a class diagram; states, transitions, and composite states for a state diagram; entities, relationships, and subgraphs for an entity relationship diagram; the slices of a pie chart (its legend entries) as nodes; the tasks and the sections of a gantt chart as nodes and subgraphs) without drawing the diagram.
Header: classDiagram and classDiagram-v2, and direction with TB, BT, LR, or RL.
Classes: class Name, a body in braces (class Name { ... }), member lines (Name : +int id), a label (class Order["Purchase order"]), names written in backticks, and classes named only by a relation.
Members: attributes and methods with the visibility +, -, #, or ~, parameters, return types, and the classifiers $ (static, underlined) and * (abstract, italic).
Generics: ~T~ in class names, members, and methods, drawn as <T>, also nested (List~List~int~~).

Annotations: <<interface>>, <<enumeration>>, and any other annotation, in a body, after the class name, or as a statement (<<service>> Service); only the first annotation of a class is drawn, as in Mermaid.
Relations: the eight kinds of relation in both directions, two-way relations, lollipop interfaces, labels (A --> B : uses), and cardinalities (A "1" --> "*" B).
Namespaces: namespace Name { ... }, nested, dotted names (namespace Geo.Plane), and a label (namespace Utils["Utility types"]).

Notes: note "text" and note for Name "text", with \n and
line breaks.

Styles: classDef (including classDef default), cssClass "A,B" name, :::, and style, with the declarations of a flowchart style; as in Mermaid, a style cannot start with a key that holds a dash, so write fill:#f9f,stroke-width:2px, not stroke-width:2px,fill:#f9f.
Interaction: click, link, and callback are read and ignored, because a picture is static.
Titles: the frontmatter title is drawn above the diagram; accTitle and accDescr are read as metadata.
Configuration: YAML frontmatter, %%{init: ...}%% directives, the five themes, themeVariables, and the class settings below, with Mermaid's precedence.
Inheritance: a solid line with a hollow triangle.
Composition: a solid line with a filled diamond.
Aggregation: a solid line with a hollow diamond.
Association: a solid line with an arrowhead.
Link: a solid line without markers.
Dependency: a dashed line with an arrowhead.
Realization: a dashed line with a hollow triangle.
Dashed link: a dashed line without markers.
Lollipop interface: a solid line to a small circle labeled with the name of the interface (Engine --() Runnable).
Two-way: a marker at both ends; any two ends combine, on a solid (--) or a dashed (..) line.
Cardinality: a quoted text before or after the line ("1", "0..1", "1..*", "many") is drawn small next to that end.
Label: the text after the colon is drawn at the middle of the line.
Leaves out the empty member compartment of a class that has no members and no methods (default false).
Makes a dotted namespace name (Geo.Plane) a namespace inside another; false draws one namespace of that name (default true).
The padding of a class box, and when it is set, of the namespaces and the notes too, which otherwise pad by 16 and 6 (default 12).
Another value selects Mermaid's legacy class diagram, which is drawn the same way (default dagre-wrapper).
The space between the classes of a rank (default 50).
The space between the ranks (default 50).
The margin above the title (default 25).
false draws the texts of the class boxes as SVG text instead of HTML labels; such a box is within a pixel of Mermaid's (default unset).
The curve of the relation lines (default basis).
Accepted, and without effect as in Mermaid; the state keys above apply instead (default unset).
Accepted, and without effect as in Mermaid (default unset).
Header: stateDiagram-v2 and stateDiagram, and direction with TB, BT, LR, or RL; the last top-level direction lays the diagram out.
States: an id (Idle), a description after a colon (Idle : waiting for input), several descriptions, state "Waiting for input" as Waiting, and states named only by a transition.
Transitions: A --> B, a label after a colon (A --> B : start), self transitions, and [*] as the start or the end state.
Composite states: state Name { ... }, nested, with their own direction and their own [*], and transitions to and from a composite state or a state inside it.
Concurrency: -- inside a composite state divides it into concurrent regions, drawn with dashed borders.
Pseudo-states: <<fork>>, <<join>>, and <<choice>>, and the forms [[fork]], [[join]], and [[choice]] (state split <<fork>>).

Notes: note left of and note right of a state, with the text after a colon or on the lines up to end note, and
line breaks; a floating note (note "text" as N) is read and not drawn, as in Mermaid.
Styles: classDef (but not classDef default, which Mermaid's grammar refuses), class A,B name, :::, and style, with the declarations of a flowchart style.
Interaction: click and click ... href are read and ignored, because a picture is static.
Titles: the frontmatter title is drawn above the diagram; accTitle and accDescr are read as metadata; hide empty description and scale are read and ignored, as in Mermaid's renderer.
Configuration: YAML frontmatter, %%{init: ...}%% directives, the five themes, themeVariables, and the state settings below, with Mermaid's precedence.
The space between the states of a rank (default 50).
The space between the ranks (default 50).
The margin above the title (default 25).
Another value selects Mermaid's legacy renderer for a stateDiagram; it is reported as mermaid-layout-unsupported and drawn the same way (default dagre-wrapper).
false draws the texts of the states as SVG text instead of HTML labels (default unset).
The curve of the transition lines (default basis).
The padding of a note (default 15).

items.term: state.padding, state.radius, and the other legacy keys
items.text: Accepted, and without effect as in Mermaid's renderer (default as in Mermaid).
No meaning for a picture (default true).
Header: erDiagram, and direction with TB, BT, LR, or RL; the last top-level direction lays the diagram out.
Entities: names, quoted names with spaces ("Entry Log"), an alias in brackets (p["Person"] or p[Person]; the first alias is kept), and entities named only by a relationship.
Relationships: A ||--o{ B : places: an entity, a cardinality, a line, a cardinality, an entity, and after the colon a role of one word or a quoted text; the cardinalities and lines are listed below.

Attributes: a block in braces after the entity (CUSTOMER { ... }), one attribute per line: a type, a name, keys (PK, FK, UK, several with commas, such as PK, FK), and a quoted comment; types such as varchar(255), string[], and decimal?; names and types in backticks; repeated blocks add to the attributes.
Generics: ~T~ in an attribute type, drawn as <T> (List~int~ is List<int>).
Subgraphs: subgraph Id["Title"] ... end, nested, with their own direction; the subgraphs are laid out in Mermaid's order, the last one first.
Styles: classDef (including classDef default), class A,B name, ::: on an entity or a relationship end, and style, with the declarations of a flowchart style.
Titles: the frontmatter title is drawn above the diagram; accTitle and accDescr are read as metadata.
Configuration: YAML frontmatter, %%{init: ...}%% directives, the five themes, themeVariables, and the entity relationship settings below, with Mermaid's precedence.

items.term: |o and o|, or the words zero or one and one or zero
items.text: Zero or one: a circle and a bar.

items.term: ||, or the words only one, one, and 1
items.text: Exactly one: two bars.

items.term: }o and o{, or the words zero or more, zero or many, many(0), 0+, and many
items.text: Zero or more: a circle and a crow's foot.

items.term: }| and |{, or the words one or more, one or many, many(1), and 1+
items.text: One or more: a bar and a crow's foot.

items.term: u, before the line only (A u--o{ B)
items.text: Parent: no marker at that end, as in Mermaid.
Identifying: a solid line.
Non-identifying: a dashed line.
Role: the word or the quoted text after the colon is drawn at the middle of the line.
The space between the entities of a rank (default 140).
The space between the ranks (default 80).
The margin above the title (default 25).
The padding added to the width of each column of a table, and around the name of an entity without attributes (default 20).
The padding added to the height of each row of a table (default 15).
The least width of an entity without attributes (default 100).
false draws the texts of the entities as SVG text instead of HTML labels; true leaves out the quarter that Mermaid adds to the paddings of a table otherwise (default unset).
Accepted, and without effect as in Mermaid's renderer (default as in Mermaid).
No meaning for a picture (default true).
Header: pie, optionally followed by showData (the legend shows each value after its label) and a title on the same line.

Slices: "label" : value, one per line: a label in double or single quotes, with backslash escapes, and a value that is a whole or a decimal number (42, 42.96); a label seen before is ignored, and a negative value is a mermaid-syntax-error, as in Mermaid.

Drawing: the slices in the order of the text, clockwise from the top, each labeled with its percentage rounded to a whole number; a slice under 1% of the total is left out of the pie and kept in the legend; the theme colors pie1 to pie12 repeat after twelve slices.
Legend: a colored square and the label of each slice, at the right of the pie unless pie.legendPosition says otherwise.
Titles: title (on its own line or after pie), else the frontmatter title, is drawn above the pie; accTitle and accDescr (on one line, or in braces over several lines) are read as metadata.
Comments: %% comments, on their own line or after a slice.

Colors: the theme variables pie1 to pie12, pieTitleTextSize, pieTitleTextColor, pieSectionTextSize, pieSectionTextColor, pieLegendTextSize, pieLegendTextColor, pieStrokeColor, pieStrokeWidth, pieOuterStrokeColor, pieOuterStrokeWidth, and pieOpacity.
Configuration: YAML frontmatter, %%{init: ...}%% directives, the five themes, themeVariables, and the pie settings below, with Mermaid's precedence.
Where the percentage labels are, as a part of the radius (0 is the center, 1 the edge) (default 0.75).
The size of a hole in the middle, as a part of the radius; a value above 0 and at most 0.9 draws a donut (default 0).
Where the legend is: right, left, top, bottom, or center (over the pie); any other value is right (default right).
The label of a slice that is drawn enlarged and opaque; hover, which enlarges the slice under the pointer in Mermaid, enlarges none in a picture (default empty).
No meaning for a picture (default true).
Header: gantt; the keywords of the statements are case-insensitive.

Tasks: Name : data, one per line; after the tags, the data is up to three fields separated by commas: an id, a start, and an end (Design :des, 2024-06-03, 5d); with two fields, a start and an end; with one field, an end, the task starting where the task before it ends.
Tags: done, active, crit, milestone, and vert before the fields, in any combination; they are listed below.
Starts: a date, or after id1 id2 (the latest end of the named tasks, which may come later in the text).
Ends: a date, a duration (a number, with a fraction if needed, and one of the units ms, s, m, h, d, w, M, and y, such as 1.5d), or until id1 id2 (the earliest start of the named tasks).

Dates: dateFormat with the dayjs tokens Mermaid loads (YYYY, MM, DD, HH, mm, X, x, and so on), read strictly; without a dateFormat, or for a date that does not match it, the ISO forms (2024-06-03, 2024-06-03T09:30); inclusiveEndDates makes an end date part of its task.

Sections: section Name groups the tasks that follow it; the sections take the theme's section colors in turn, and
breaks a section name into lines.

Excluded days: excludes with weekends, day names (monday), and dates; includes with dates that are worked anyway; weekend friday or weekend saturday (the default) for the first day of the weekend; a task whose end is a duration grows over the excluded days, which are shaded.

Axis: axisFormat with the d3 time format directives (%b %e, %H:%M, and so on), tickInterval (a number and one of millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, and month, such as 1week), and weekday (the first day of the week for weekly ticks); gantt.topAxis draws a second axis at the top (the topAxis statement fails in Mermaid, and is a mermaid-syntax-error here).
Compact mode: displayMode: compact in the frontmatter, or gantt.displayMode, puts the tasks of a section on as few rows as keep them apart.
Today: todayMarker off, or todayMarker with a style (stroke-width:5px,stroke:#0f0); the today line is drawn only when the caller gives the time (MermaidRenderOptions.Now).
Interaction: click id href "url" and click id call fn(args) are read and never drawn as links, because a picture is static; the text of a task with a click is drawn bold, as in Mermaid.
Titles: title, else the frontmatter title, is drawn above the chart; accTitle and accDescr are read as metadata.

Colors: the theme variables taskBkgColor, taskBorderColor, taskTextColor, taskTextDarkColor, taskTextOutsideColor, taskTextClickableColor, activeTaskBkgColor, activeTaskBorderColor, doneTaskBkgColor, doneTaskBorderColor, critBkgColor, critBorderColor, sectionBkgColor, sectionBkgColor2, altSectionBkgColor, excludeBkgColor, gridColor, todayLineColor, vertLineColor, and titleColor.
Configuration: YAML frontmatter, %%{init: ...}%% directives, the five themes, themeVariables, and the gantt settings below, with Mermaid's precedence.
A finished task: a bar in the theme's doneTaskBkgColor.
A task in progress: a bar in activeTaskBkgColor.
A critical task: a bar in critBkgColor with a critBorderColor border, or with done or active, in their color with that border.
A diamond the height of a bar at the middle of the task, so a milestone of 0d is at its start.
A vertical line over every row at the start of the task, with its name below the rows.
The height of a bar (default 20).
The space between two rows (default 4).
The space above the first row and below the last (default 50).
The space left of the time axis, where the section names are (default 75).
The space right of the time axis (default 75).
The top of the grid lines and of a vertical marker (default 35).
The baseline of the title (default 25).
The font size of the task texts (default 11).
The font size of the section names (default 11).
The number of section colors that repeat (default 4).
The format of the axis labels of a chart without axisFormat (default %Y-%m-%d).
The interval of the ticks of a chart without tickInterval (default unset).
true draws a second axis at the top (default false).
compact puts the tasks of a section on as few rows as keep them apart (default empty).
The width of the chart; unset is 784, the width Mermaid takes in the page of mmdc (default unset).
Accepted, and without effect as in Mermaid; the weekday statement applies (default sunday).
No meaning for a picture (default true).
The diagram type is not drawn by this version (every type but flowchart, graph, sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, stateDiagram, erDiagram, pie, and gantt); the picture is empty.

Every other diagram type is recognized: info reports it with "supported": false, and render writes an empty picture of 16 by 16 pixels with the diagnostic mermaid-diagram-unsupported (--strict makes it an unsupported-feature failure). Mindmap diagrams are planned later.
An icon (fa:fa-car in a label, an @{ icon: ... } node, an icon in the properties of a sequence participant); the node or participant keeps its shape and label without the icon.
Math ($$...$$, drawn by KaTeX in Mermaid) in a sequence diagram; the text is drawn as written.
A look other than classic (handDrawn, neo); the diagram is drawn classic.

A layout other than dagre (elk, also the flowchart-elk keyword), or a state.defaultRenderer that selects Mermaid's legacy state renderer; the diagram is laid out with dagre, and a legacy state diagram is drawn as a stateDiagram-v2.
A themeCSS rule whose selector is not one of the diagram's own (such as .node rect in a flowchart), an at-rule, or a nested rule; the rule is not applied.

The theme: default, base, dark, forest, or neutral, like mmdc -t. A theme the diagram sets in its frontmatter or a directive still wins. In a link or an input path the fragment theme=dark does the same (flow.mmd#theme=dark). On any other kind of input --theme is a usage-error.

The natural size is Mermaid's SVG view box in pixels; --scale, --width, and --height draw the diagram sharply at another size (a diagram larger than {{maxDimension}} pixels on a side needs one of them).
The color under the diagram: white by default, transparent keeps the transparency of Mermaid's own SVG.
Every unsupported construct, and a picture that is not drawn, becomes an unsupported-feature error.
The code of every warning of a diagram; the specific mermaid-* code is in detail and the line and column in location.
Error (mermaid-error): a shape name Mermaid does not define; the hint names the nearest one.
Error (mermaid-error): the text does not follow the grammar of its diagram type; the message gives the line, the column, and the tokens that were expected, and the hint suggests the fix.
Error (mermaid-error): the first statement is not a Mermaid diagram keyword; the hint names the nearest one.
Error (mermaid-error): the frontmatter or the shape data is not valid YAML; anchors, aliases, and tags are refused (mermaid-yaml-unsupported).
Error (budget-exceeded): a limit of the library (nodes, edges, nesting, label length, layout work, pictures, painted pixels); see 'canvasnet help limits'.

Error (mermaid-error): the diagram cannot be laid out, for example a subgraph that contains itself, an empty sequence block, two composite states that contain each other, or a gantt task whose date is invalid or whose after and until references go in a circle.
Warning: a sequence participant has a type Mermaid does not define; it is not drawn, as in Mermaid, and the hint names the nearest type.
Warning: a configuration key Mermaid does not define; it is ignored.
Warning: a configuration value of the wrong type or range, or a theme that is not available; it is ignored (sequence.textPlacement: fo is drawn with the default placement).
Warning: the text tried to change a secure key (securityLevel, maxTextSize, maxEdges, and so on); the change is ignored.
Warning: a style declaration outside the supported subset; it is ignored.
Warning: an HTML tag outside the supported label subset; the tag is dropped and its text is kept.
Warning: a picture the resolver did not give; the node keeps its frame.
A link that is not drawn (a missing file, a path outside the folder, a network URL) is the warning svg-image-unresolved with the reason, and --strict makes it a failure.
Warning: a character that no bundled font has (for example CJK); it is drawn as the missing-glyph box.

Warning: a gantt chart needs today (a todayMarker style, an after or until id that no task has, or a date without a year, month, or day) and MermaidRenderOptions.Now is not set; the today line is not drawn and 1970-01-01 is taken as today.
Warning: the tickInterval of a gantt chart would make more than 10,000 ticks; the default ticks are drawn, as in Mermaid.
Warning: the tasks of a gantt chart with excluded days span more than five years; the excluded days are not shaded, as in Mermaid.
Warning: more reports than MaxDiagnostics; the rest are dropped.
A text longer than {{mmdMaxTextSize}} characters is corrupt-input.

Text is measured and drawn with the bundled Liberation Sans (Mermaid's default trebuchet ms, verdana, and arial map to it) and the bundled Noto fallback fonts, never an installed font, so the result does not depend on the machine; against Mermaid rendered with the same font the layout matches to a hundredth of a pixel.
The circles of the new shapes are true circles where Mermaid draws rough.js curves (a few hundredths of a pixel).
The picture is static: no interaction, and an animated edge is drawn as its first frame.

info lays the diagram out without the pictures of its nodes (it reads no other file), so a picture node without w and h can make the drawn diagram a little larger or smaller than the size info reports (with --width or --height it is fitted into the box); give an @{ img } node its w and h (constraint on) so that the layout does not depend on the picture. A render without --width and --height reports the natural size of the diagram it drew (the natural size of render --json); a library render of the diagram file without a size (CanvasNetViewer.Render) also charges its pixel budget for that drawn size, while a document that embeds the diagram always gives it a size.
A diagram is drawn over white unless --background says otherwise (Mermaid's SVG is transparent); as a picture in an SVG file it stays transparent.

Mermaid crashes on some invalid graphs (a subgraph cycle, a link to a subgraph without an anchor, two composite states that contain each other, a note on a state that appears nowhere before it, a relationship to an entity named like a subgraph declared after it, a relationship from a subgraph to an entity inside it); these are a located mermaid-error instead.

Interaction (click, href, call, tooltips, the link and callback of a class diagram, and the click of a state diagram or a gantt chart) is read and ignored without a report, because a picture is static.

Mermaid draws a broken sequence diagram or fails for an empty block (a block with no message or note inside), for link or links on an actor, boundary, control, or entity participant, and for a properties icon that is not text; these are a located mermaid-render-failed instead.
$$ math is drawn and measured as written (mermaid-math-unsupported), and textPlacement: fo (HTML labels) is drawn with the default placement.
The color keywords and system colors of a box or a rect background take the values of headless Chrome in the light scheme (system colors depend on the platform in a browser).

The width of a text is the advance of its glyphs grown to the pixels its first and last glyphs reach, as Chrome measures it; for fonts or sizes other than those of the reference diagrams, a width can differ by a pixel, which can move the margins by up to a pixel.

With htmlLabels: false the texts of a class box are SVG text, measured as Chrome measures them; Chrome's box of a few glyphs at the end of a text is a pixel wider, so such a class box can differ from Mermaid's by up to a pixel.
Mermaid's fix-up of an SVG class text that holds &gt (a generic) is not ported; the entities are decoded instead, which gives the same characters for a text of one line.
$$ math in a class text is drawn and measured as written, without a report.
A style declaration of a class, state, or entity relationship diagram outside the supported subset is reported at the first mention of the class, state, or entity, not at the style statement.
A corner radius (rx or ry) in a style, a classDef, or themeCSS is ignored with a mermaid-style-ignored warning; the radii of Mermaid's own style sheet are drawn.
The texts of class and state diagrams are always cleaned as at Mermaid's strict level; securityLevel changes nothing.

Mermaid's legacy state renderer is not ported: a stateDiagram with another state.defaultRenderer is drawn with the current renderer and reported as mermaid-layout-unsupported at the state key of the configuration.
The direction info reports for a state or entity relationship diagram is the last top-level direction statement, the one the diagram is laid out in, where Mermaid's getDirection gives the first.
The last concurrent region of a composite state has the id id-random-N where Mermaid's id holds a random number; the id is never drawn.
Mermaid's entity relationship markers clip the line at the edge of their view port, which hides half of the stroke at the tip; the clip is not modeled, so a tip can be half a stroke longer.
With htmlLabels: false the texts of an entity table take the style sheet's label color (nodeTextColor, else textColor), where Chrome uses textColor; the two are the same in the built-in themes.
The marker shapes of the neo look and the entity colors of the redux themes are not drawn (the look is reported, and the themes are not available).

The today of a gantt chart is the time the caller gives (MermaidRenderOptions.Now), never the clock; the tool, the Viewer, and the Pandoc filter give none, so the today line is not drawn and 1970-01-01 is taken as today (mermaid-gantt-today-unavailable where it matters). Write todayMarker off, or give the dates in full, to keep the warning away.
The dates of a gantt chart are in UTC, where Mermaid uses the time zone of the browser, so a chart never changes with the machine or with daylight saving time.
A gantt date that matches neither the dateFormat nor an ISO form (2024-1-5, Jan 5 2024, which browsers read in their own ways) is a located mermaid-render-failed Invalid date.

Mermaid fails, or draws a broken chart, for the topAxis statement, a task whose data holds only tags, a first task without a start, a task with more than three fields, after or until references that go in a circle, excluded days that never end, a compact section named like a JavaScript object member (constructor, toString), and a dateFormat with the week (w, ww, wo, gggg) or zone name (z, zzz) tokens; these are a located mermaid-syntax-error or mermaid-render-failed instead.

A gantt chart is 784 pixels wide, the width Mermaid takes in the page of mmdc, unless gantt.useWidth is set (in a browser it takes the width of the page), and its ticks keep d3's half-pixel offset at every scale.

The opacity of a pie slice, a gantt section row, and the gantt grid is folded into its colors, so where two of them overlap the colors can differ slightly; the turn of a milestone and the enlargement of a highlighted slice are applied to the outline, and the crisp edges of the gantt grid are drawn antialiased.
A character that no bundled font has is drawn as the missing-glyph box in a pie or gantt text without the warning mermaid-text-missing-glyph.
The links of a gantt chart (click ... href) are always checked as at Mermaid's strict level and kept only as data.
